Your job is to find COUNTER-EVIDENCE: anywhere the project's own integration docs say something is ALREADY CONFIRMED, RESOLVED, PROVIDED, IN-HAND, or DECIDED — i.e. NOT actually outstanding.

Read every file in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/integration/ (files 01 through 18, plus index.md).

For EACH integration (SFCC, Contentful, MuleSoft, Omneo, GiveX, Booxi, Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize, Vimeo), report with FILE PATH + LINE NUMBERS:

1. Any specific vendor ID / account ID / container ID / project ID / merchant ID / key / host / URL that the doc states is ALREADY KNOWN or CONFIRMED (quote the value and the confirmation date if given). E.g. "GTM container confirmed as X", "prod host confirmed as ruffles.zimmermann.com", "Optimizely project ID single across envs".
2. Any DECISION the doc records as already MADE (e.g. consent approach chosen, video platform confirmed, gift-card provider decided, a Didomi category confirmed).
3. The exact "Open items requiring client confirmation" list for that integration (section 11 usually) — just the item titles/first line, with line numbers.
4. Any statement that a credential is PUBLIC / ships-in-bundle / server-side-only (affects whether it's really a "blocker").

Be precise with line numbers — I need path:line citations. Do not summarize away specifics like IDs, hosts, dates. Report per-integration. Do not edit anything.

1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
11	- Basket and cart
12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
16	
17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
18	
19	Out of scope of this document:
20	
21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
25	
26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
30	        │
31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
32	        ▼
33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
35	        ▼
36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	SFCC realm
40	```
41	
42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
45	
46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
47	
48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
53	
54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
55	
56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
57	
58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
59	
60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
61	
62	- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
63	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
64	- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
65	- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.
66	
67	## 4. Data exchanged
68	
69	| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
70	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
72	| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
73	| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
74	| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
75	| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76	| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77	| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78	| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79	
80	Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81	
82	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83	
84	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88	
89	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
90	
91	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
92	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
93	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
94	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
95	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
96	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
97	
98	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
99	
100	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
101	
102	| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
104	| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
105	| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
106	| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
107	| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
108	| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
109	| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
110	| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
111	| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
112	
113	- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
114	- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
115	- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.
116	
117	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
118	
119	| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
120	| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
121	| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
122	| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
123	| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
124	| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
125	| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
126	| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
127	| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
128	| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |
129	
130	## 9. Security and privacy
131	
132	- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
133	- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
134	- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
135	- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.
136	
137	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
138	
139	1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.
140	
141	2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) holds `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl`'s origin in a pool separate from `sfcc-scapi` (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). That separation only provides blast-radius isolation if the two hosts are different origins. If `sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to the same SCAPI host, the pools should be merged.
142

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
62	        │
63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
65	        │
66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
69	```
70	
71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
84	
85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
86	
87	## 5. Data exchanged
88	
89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
96	
97	No PII flows through Contentful.
98	
99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
100	
101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
107	
108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
109	
110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
113	
114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
115	
116	| Failure | Behaviour |
117	|---|---|
118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
125	
126	## 9. Security and privacy
127	
128	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
129	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
130	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
131	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
132	
133	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
134	
135	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
136	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
137	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
138

1	# 03 — MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads via MRT proxy)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	MuleSoft is the integration middleware that sits between SFCC and Zimmermann's back-office systems (NewStore OMS, AP21, Omneo, Narvar). The vast majority of MuleSoft traffic is server-to-server from SFCC and is out of scope here. This document covers the **separate, direct path** in which the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer calls MuleSoft directly via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of read operations where SFCC adds no value to the round-trip.
6	
7	Operations in scope of this document (PWA → MRT → MuleSoft, with SFCC outside the read path):
8	
9	- Order history list (CRM-056 / CRM-057, RRC-013) — the 50 most recent orders, online and in-store
10	- Order detail (CRM-071 / CRM-072)
11	- Account dashboard "recent orders" summary (CRM-029, OM-017, OM-035)
12	- Returns data for the My Account returns view (CRM-088)
13	- Real-time stock availability:
14	  - Find in Boutique flyout and BOPIS boutique selection screen (CFD-043, CAI-038)
15	  - Collect in Boutique store + size validation (CAI-043)
16	  - Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034 — this MuleSoft flow does not yet exist; the storefront falls back to the inventory feed until it is built)
17	- GiveX balance check (GC-037, GC-053) — MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX TCP connection and credentials
18	
19	Operations out of scope (server-to-server, outside the PWA layer):
20	
21	- SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore order creation and fulfilment writes
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo customer / loyalty / address sync
23	- SFCC → MuleSoft → AP21 retail rewards balance lookup
24	- Product and pricing master feed AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (catalogue and pricebooks)
25	- The daily and 15-minute inventory feeds NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC (CAI-019, CAI-020)
26	- Adyen fraud webhooks via MuleSoft (PAY-046)
27	- GiveX validate / redeem / refund (server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX)
28	- GiveX gift-card **issuance** at purchase (SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX)
29	
30	## 2. PWA-layer architecture
31	
32	The flow below reflects the confirmed design from the MuleSoft integration PDFs (Jun 2025). MRT authenticates to MuleSoft using platform credentials (`client_id` + `client_secret`). The `customer_id` is passed as a plain UUID query parameter; MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer.
33	
34	```
35	Browser (My Account, cart, BOPIS flyout, etc.)
36	        │  Authenticated customer — customer_id known from SFCC session
37	        ▼
38	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/<endpoint>
39	        │
40	        ▼
41	MRT Node layer:
42	   1. Reads customer_id from the authenticated SFCC session
43	   2. Appends client_id + client_secret as HTTP request headers (MRT environment variables)
44	   3. Forwards to https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api[-{env}]/<path>
45	      (env suffix: `-dev` for Dev, `-qa` for QA; no suffix for Prod — per vendor docs)
46	      with customer_id as a query parameter
47	        │
48	        ▼
49	MuleSoft (Magento Experience API):
50	   • Verifies channel auth via client_id + client_secret
51	   • Does NOT verify shopper identity at the transport layer
52	   • Routes internally to the Order Transactions Sync Process API → NewStore
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	NewStore response → MuleSoft → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields needed)
56	```
57	
58	- The browser never carries MuleSoft credentials. `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and are never exposed to the browser bundle.
59	- `customer_id` is a UUID string. MRT reads it from the authenticated SFCC session (step 1 above) — never from browser-supplied input. This prevents a browser from retrieving another customer's data by substituting a different UUID.
60	
61	## 3. Endpoint inventory
62	
63	Endpoints marked ✅ have confirmed paths and response schemas from the MuleSoft technical design documents. Endpoints marked ⏳ are working assumptions pending the formal OpenAPI specification (open item 1 in §9).
64	
65	| Endpoint | Status | Used by | Backed by | Requirement |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| `GET /api/orders?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | Order history list (My Account) | NewStore | CRM-056, CRM-057, OM-035, RRC-013 |
68	| `GET /api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | ✅ | Order detail page | NewStore | CRM-071, CRM-072 |
69	| `GET /api/returns?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | My Account returns view | NewStore Returns API | CRM-088, RRC-007 |
70	| `POST /api/find-in-store` body: `{ProductId, CountryCode}` | ✅ | Find in Boutique flyout + BOPIS screen | NewStore | CFD-043, CAI-038 |
71	| Orders list with `count=3` — confirm path with integration team | ⏳ | Account dashboard summary | NewStore | CRM-029 |
72	| GiveX balance check — path TBC; flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool) | ⏳ | Gift card balance in My Account and at checkout | GiveX via MuleSoft | GC-037, GC-053 |
73	| Collect in Boutique validation — path TBC | ⏳ | Collect in Boutique store + size validation | NewStore | CAI-043 |
74	| Cart → checkout entry stock check — MuleSoft flow not yet built | ⏳ | Cart → checkout entry | NewStore | CAI-034 |
75	
76	The full OpenAPI specification is open item 1 in §9.
77	
78	## 4. Authentication and credentials
79	
80	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `client_id` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
83	| `client_secret` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
84	| `customer_id` (UUID) | Plain query parameter on orders / returns calls; read from the SFCC session server-side | Not a secret — MRT enforces it matches the authenticated session |
85	
86	One `client_id` / `client_secret` pair per environment. Credential rotation is owned by the integration team.
87	
88	## 5. Data exchanged
89	
90	| Direction | Data | Notes |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| Browser → MRT | Authenticated customer session (customer_id extracted server-side); endpoint path; small query/body payload where applicable | The browser never sees MuleSoft credentials. |
93	| MRT → MuleSoft | `client_id` + `client_secret` (channel auth); `customer_id` as a query parameter; endpoint payload | `client_id`/`client_secret` authorise the channel. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer. |
94	| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — order summary, order detail, boutique stock list, returns list | MRT projects only the fields the UI consumes to keep payload small. |
95	
96	No PII flows back to the browser beyond what the customer already owns (their own order data, their own returns). Boutique stock responses contain no PII.
97	
98	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
99	
100	- All MuleSoft reads are made only when the relevant route or interaction triggers them. The order-history list does not preload on home; the boutique inventory call only fires when the Find in Boutique flyout opens (CAI-038).
101	- The MuleSoft vendor response time target (per the received PDFs) is < 2.5 s. The PWA's own soft-failure threshold of 2 s (see §7) is intentionally stricter.
102	- Working performance budget (working assumption — pending SLA confirmation with the integration team): p95 under 800 ms for order list and order detail; under 500 ms for boutique inventory checks.
103	- TanStack Query caches order list and order detail responses on the client; stale data is acceptable for the dashboard summary and order list but never for cart → checkout entry stock checks, which always re-fetch.
104	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the MuleSoft host is emitted from the My Account entry routes once the customer is authenticated.
105	
106	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
107	
108	| Failure | Behaviour |
109	|---|---|
110	| MuleSoft rejects channel auth (invalid `client_id`/`client_secret`) | Return 401 to the browser. This indicates a misconfigured or rotated credential — requires an ops fix, not a user retry. Surface a generic error UI. |
111	| MuleSoft 5xx on order list | Order history view shows an explicit retry UI. The contract is "explicit retry, never partial data". |
112	| MuleSoft 5xx on cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) | Block checkout entry with a clear error. Do not silently progress; a stale stock decision risks an oversell. |
113	| MuleSoft 5xx on Find in Boutique inventory (CFD-043) | Show "Stock information temporarily unavailable" inside the flyout and a retry CTA. Do not fall back to cached data — boutique stock is real-time by design. |
114	| MuleSoft 5xx on Collect in Boutique validation (CAI-043) | Reject the boutique selection with an error; the shopper can pick a different store or method. |
115	| MuleSoft timeout above 2 seconds | Treated as a soft failure. UI degrades gracefully per the rows above. |
116	| NewStore upstream of MuleSoft is down | Surfaced to the storefront as a MuleSoft 5xx. Same handling. |
117	
118	## 8. Security and privacy
119	
120	- `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and never appear in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or client-accessible logs.
121	- All MRT → MuleSoft traffic is over TLS 1.2+.
122	- `customer_id` is a plain UUID query parameter passed to MuleSoft. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer — MuleSoft trusts the channel. Impersonation is prevented at the MRT layer: MRT reads `customer_id` from the authenticated SFCC session only, never from browser-supplied input.
123	- No PII is logged at the MRT layer beyond a request ID and the endpoint name.
124	
125	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
126	
127	1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
128	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
129	3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).

1	# 04 — Omneo (Communication Preferences iFrame)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Omneo is the system of record for customer identity and loyalty. Most Omneo traffic is server-to-server via SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo and is out of scope here. The only surface where the PWA storefront talks to Omneo directly is a single embedded iFrame inside My Account (CRM-174 – CRM-177). The iFrame is the confirmed PRD approach (CRM-174 — enhancement logged to move into SFCC). Per CRM-174, the iFrame currently contains:
6	
7	- **Communication Preferences** — the customer views and updates marketing and service preferences (CRM-175, CRM-176).
8	- **Region/country selection** — allows the customer to select location, state, and language preference.
9	- **Three clickable images** that open the respective PLP within the iFrame itself; this PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is logged in the Enhancement Log and is not in scope at launch.
10	
11	Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. Omneo's documented embed is, however, a Shopify theme extension; the gating question for this non-Shopify (PWA) build is the auth handshake, covered in §9 (Open items).
12	
13	In scope:
14	
15	- The Communication Preferences iFrame and its host page on My Account
16	- Issuance of the customer-scoped credential that authorises the iFrame
17	- Embedding, sizing, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser
18	
19	Out of scope of this document (handled server-side, outside the PWA layer):
20	
21	- Profile, address book, order history, loyalty reads and writes
22	- The DMU-004 "profile read from Omneo at login" round trip — load-bearing, but executed by SFCC; the PWA only consumes the resulting customer object via the Commerce SDK
23	- The Omneo → Emarsys email-marketing handoff
24	
25	The Zimmermann CRM team owns the preference categories, labels, and translations rendered inside the widget. The storefront embeds the widget only — no preference business logic lives in the storefront.
26	
27	## 2. Browser-side architecture
28	
29	```
30	My Account → "Communication Preferences" route
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	Server (SSR or MRT endpoint):
34	  • Reads the authenticated SFCC customer
35	  • Mints a customer-scoped credential for the embed. The exact handshake
36	    is unconfirmed (§9); the two candidate mechanisms are:
37	        (a) signed URL / HMAC — signature = HMAC-SHA256( customerId, omneo_secret )
38	        (b) a server-minted, short-lived, profile-scoped JWT (an Omneo
39	            IDToken), obtained by a trusted backend calling Omneo's auth
40	            endpoint with an admin token, then handed to the browser
41	  • Returns the iFrame URL (and, for (b), the IDToken) to the client
42	        │
43	        ▼
44	Browser renders the iFrame against the Omneo host, carrying whichever
45	customer-scoped credential the confirmed handshake requires
46	        │
47	        ▼
48	Omneo iFrame:
49	  • Validates the credential, opens a scoped session for that profile only
50	  • Reads and writes preferences directly against Omneo
51	  • On save, Omneo emits a webhook to SFCC via MuleSoft (CRM-177);
52	    SFCC reflects the new state on the next Commerce SDK customer read
53	```
54	
55	- The iFrame is rendered only for authenticated customers on the Communication Preferences route. There is no guest path.
56	- The credential is minted on the server so that neither an HMAC secret nor an Omneo admin token ever reaches the browser bundle or enters the React component tree as a build-time value — regardless of which handshake is confirmed.
57	- Saves originate inside the iFrame and write directly to Omneo (CRM-176). The PWA does not POST preference data itself.
58	- The PWA does not attempt to read or scrape the iFrame DOM — it is cross-origin and a hard boundary. State reflection in SFCC is handled by the webhook flow.
59	
60	## 3. Authentication and credentials
61	
62	- **Auth pattern (unconfirmed — see §9):** the embed is authorised by a customer-scoped credential minted server-side. The exact mechanism for a non-Shopify (PWA) embed is not confirmed; two candidates are carried:
63	  - **(a) Signed URL / HMAC** — `customerId` plus an HMAC-SHA256 signature of that ID using an Omneo-issued secret. This is the approach this document originally assumed.
64	  - **(b) Server-minted profile-scoped JWT (`IDToken`)** — a trusted backend calls Omneo's auth endpoint with an admin token to mint a short-lived, profile-scoped JWT, which is then handed to the browser for the embed. This is the mechanism Omneo's developer docs ("Using Omneo ID") actually document; note it is explicitly not an HMAC. (HMAC appears in Omneo's docs only for Shopify app-proxy request signing, a separate Shopify-only concern.)
65	- **Customer ID source:** the Omneo customer ID is stored on the SFCC customer record alongside the email at migration (DMU-004); under (a) it is the value signed by the HMAC, and under (b) it scopes the minted JWT. The SFCC customer ID and the customer email are not used as the credential input.
66	- **Secret / token location:** whichever credential the confirmed handshake requires (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is held in SFCC Business Manager alongside the rest of the SFCC ↔ Omneo credentials, and the minting is performed server-side (e.g. an SCAPI custom endpoint). This keeps all Omneo credentials in one place and reuses the existing rotation procedure. (Contingent on the embed mechanism confirmed in §9.)
67	- **No Omneo credential in the browser bundle.** The browser only ever receives the assembled URL and, under (b), a short-lived customer-scoped token — never the HMAC secret or the admin token.
68	- **Credential freshness:** the credential is regenerated on every visit to the Communication Preferences route — it is not cached in the SCAPI response body, not persisted, and not stored in `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`. A minted JWT is additionally short-lived by design.
69	- **ITP / ETP resilience:** anti-tracking browsers (Safari ITP, Firefox ETP) may block third-party cookies inside the iFrame. Because auth is carried in the URL (or, under (b), in a URL parameter), cookie blocking does not break the experience.
70	
71	## 4. Data exchanged
72	
73	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Browser → SFCC | Authenticated customer's SLAS access token | Standard Commerce SDK request |
76	| SFCC → Browser | Assembled iFrame URL containing the customer-scoped credential (exact form TBC — see §9) | JSON response to the route loader |
77	| Browser → Omneo | iFrame load (HTTP GET to Omneo host) | `<iframe src>` |
78	| Omneo backend ↔ Omneo iFrame | Preference reads and writes | Owned by Omneo |
79	| Omneo → SFCC | Updated preferences via webhook through MuleSoft (CRM-177) | Out of band — not visible to the storefront |
80	
81	No marketing-preference payload crosses the storefront boundary. The PWA is a pure transport for the assembled iFrame URL.
82	
83	## 5. Performance and loading strategy
84	
85	- The Communication Preferences route is route-level code-split. The iFrame component is dynamically imported and is not part of any other route bundle.
86	- The `<iframe>` element is rendered with `loading="lazy"` and only after the credential-mint round trip resolves. A skeleton placeholder reserves the eventual iFrame height to avoid layout shift.
87	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Omneo iFrame host is emitted on the My Account routes only, not site-wide.
88	- The widget's own payload is owned by Omneo and is not counted against the storefront bundle budget, but the LCP of the surrounding My Account page must remain within the storefront's LCP budget (≤ 2 s at p75 mobile).
89	
90	## 6. Multi-region behaviour
91	
92	- A single Omneo tenant serves all eight storefronts. Locale is passed as a query-string parameter on the iFrame URL.
93	- The widget displays in the storefront's active locale (English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic).
94	- Per-region differences in available preference categories (e.g. SMS opt-in only in some regions) are configured inside Omneo, not in the PWA.
95	- The US domestic pre-checked marketing opt-in default (REG-057) applies at registration and footer-form entry points, not inside this widget; the widget surfaces only the current state of preferences for an existing customer.
96	
97	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
98	
99	| Failure | Behaviour |
100	|---|---|
101	| Credential-mint round trip fails (SFCC unreachable or signing endpoint errors) | Render an explicit retry UI on the Communication Preferences page. Do not render the iFrame with a stale or unsigned URL. Per the TSD graceful-degradation contract for Omneo: never render partial data. |
102	| URL is assembled but the iFrame fails to load (CSP violation, Omneo CDN outage, network block) | Show a retry CTA inside the iFrame slot. After two consecutive failures, surface a contact-support message and a link to the storefront's privacy/contact page so the customer can manage preferences via support. (Design decision — exact fallback UX not specified in CRM-174–177; confirm with UX/product.) |
103	| iFrame loads but an Omneo-internal save fails | Owned by the widget's own UX — the PWA does not intercept. |
104	| Customer is unauthenticated when navigating to the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No credential-mint request is issued. |
105	| Omneo rotates or revokes the customer-auth credential (HMAC secret or Omneo admin token, depending on the confirmed handshake) | Rotation is handled in SFCC BM by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |
106	
107	## 8. Security and privacy
108	
109	- A single customer-scoped credential, minted server-side, is the entire auth surface presented to Omneo. Which credential that is depends on the handshake confirmed in §9 — either an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the customer ID, or a server-minted short-lived profile-scoped JWT (`IDToken`). The underlying secret (the HMAC secret, or the Omneo admin token used to mint the JWT) is stored in SFCC BM, never in the PWA bundle, never logged, and rotated per the standard SFCC credential rotation policy.
110	- The `<iframe>` element uses the minimum `sandbox` flags required for the widget to function — at minimum `allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`, and `allow-same-origin`. The exact final set is confirmed during integration testing against the live Omneo widget.
111	- `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` is set on the `<iframe>` so the customer's storefront URL does not appear in Omneo's referer logs.
112	- Omneo's host is added to the storefront `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` directives. No wildcard Omneo subdomain is allowed.
113	- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), the customer record is removed from SFCC and Omneo through the SFCC GDPR cartridge and the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo chain. The Communication Preferences widget itself has no separate erasure flow.
114	
115	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
116	
117	No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.
118	
119	1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is an Omneo iFrame embedded in My Account, and Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the iframe embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. Per the updated CRM-174, the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection, and clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (the PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is logged as an enhancement and is not in scope at launch). However, Omneo's documented embed is a **Shopify theme app extension** that authenticates the logged-in customer via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy (a token fetched from the Shopify storefront session) — auth plumbing that does not exist in a PWA. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: (a) the Profile Portal embed URL and how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it; and (b) the auth handshake outside Shopify — whether it is the customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach this document assumes, or a server-minted customer-scoped Omneo token. If neither embed path is available on the plan, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted Profile Portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
120	2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
121	   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
122	   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
123	   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
124	3. **Customer-auth credential — Omneo admin token (for IDToken minting).** Provide the per-environment Omneo admin token used server-side to mint a customer-scoped IDToken (short-lived JWT) for the iFrame auth handshake. (Note: HMAC signing is a Shopify-specific Omneo pattern; the assumed path for a PWA is server-minted IDToken — confirm with Omneo.) Without it the Omneo iFrame authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

1	# 05 — GiveX (Gift Cards)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	GiveX is Zimmermann's gift card and credit note processor. This document covers the PWA surfaces that directly call GiveX via MRT:
6	
7	- The **balance-check input** in My Account (GC-051–062) and the "Check Balance" link in the checkout gift card entry field (GC-037). Both use the same MRT endpoint: `POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance`.
8	- The **gift card purchase experience** (§12) — the PWA renders the product, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists them on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side and is not a PWA-direct call.
9	
10	Out of scope (server-side, not a PWA-direct path):
11	
12	- Gift card and credit note validate / redeem / refund at checkout (GC-034–049) — handled via the NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX. The PWA sees only the resulting payment-instrument state from SCAPI.
13	- Gift card issuance at purchase — SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX.
14	- GiveX validate / redeem / refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44).
15	- Reversal on capture failure — handled server-side by NewStore / SFCC.
16	
17	## 2. Vendor relationship
18	
19	GiveX is reached via MuleSoft — the PWA never holds a GiveX credential or makes a direct GiveX call. For the balance check, MuleSoft owns the GiveX socket, host failover, and credentials internally; the PWA calls MuleSoft over HTTPS. Redemption at checkout goes via the NewStore adaptor through MuleSoft, outside the PWA boundary.
20	
21	## 3. PWA-layer architecture
22	
23	```
24	My Account (GC-051) / Checkout "Check Balance" link (GC-037)
25	        │
26	        ▼
27	Customer enters gift card or credit note number and PIN
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Browser: POST /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/givex/balance
31	   body: { number, pin }
32	        │
33	        ▼
34	MRT Node layer:
35	   1. Applies rate-limit and bot protection on this route
36	      (no per-customer cap — GC-062 — but route is hardened
37	       with WAF / bot management / rate-limit / CAPTCHA per
38	       GiveX security guidance)
39	   2. Forwards over HTTPS to MuleSoft with the MuleSoft API token
40	      held as an MRT environment variable
41	        │
42	        ▼
43	MuleSoft → GiveX (internal — MuleSoft's responsibility)
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	MuleSoft → MRT → Browser:
47	   { maskedNumber, balance, currency, expiry, error? }
48	        │
49	        ▼
50	PWA renders the result inline beside the input (GC-054, GC-055)
51	```
52	
53	The browser never sees a GiveX credential or raw GiveX error. It sees only an HTTPS request to the storefront's own MRT origin and a typed JSON response.
54	
55	Both the My Account balance check and the checkout Check Balance link (GC-037) use the same MRT endpoint. Login is not required for either (GC-059).
56	
57	The balance check requires both the card number and its PIN, for both gift cards and credit notes. Zimmermann's GiveX merchant program has secure PINs enabled, so the PIN field is mandatory on every request. The PIN is a payment credential — see §9.
58	
59	The customer can check another card or credit note without leaving the page (GC-055). The same input field accepts both gift card and credit note numbers (GC-057).
60	
61	## 4. Authentication and credentials
62	
63	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| MuleSoft API token | MRT environment variable; injected on outbound request | Secret — never reaches the browser |
66	
67	The customer is not required to be authenticated (GC-059). The call is not bound to a SLAS JWT.
68	
69	## 5. Data exchanged
70	
71	| Direction | Data | Notes |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| Browser → MRT | Card or credit note number and PIN — POST body only, never a query string | Both are payment credentials; not logged, not stored beyond the request |
74	| MRT → MuleSoft | Number, PIN, and MuleSoft API token | HTTPS |
75	| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Masked card serial, balance, currency, expiry, mapped error code | Only the serial portion is returned; prefix and check digit are dropped by MuleSoft |
76	
77	The full card number and PIN are treated as payment credentials and are handled as described in §9.
78	
79	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
80	
81	- The route is reached only when the customer submits the form — no upfront script load.
82	- Working performance target: p95 under 1.5 seconds including the GiveX round-trip via MuleSoft. Hard timeout at 5 seconds (§8).
83	
84	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
85	
86	- The balance check is available on all storefronts — domestic and international (GC-051–062 scope).
87	- Currency in the response is whatever GiveX returns for the card. The storefront formats it per the active locale without converting.
88	
89	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
90	
91	| Failure | Behaviour |
92	|---|---|
93	| GiveX does not recognise the card number | Display the error from GiveX (GC-056) — no inline pre-submission validation. |
94	| Card expired or zero balance | Show the appropriate error message (GC-060). |
95	| MuleSoft returns an error after exhausting failover | "Balance check is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." (GC-061). Shopper can retry; subject to rate-limit. |
96	| MRT timeout above 5 seconds | Same handling as MuleSoft error above. |
97	| Rate-limit triggered | Generic retry-later message. Do not disclose the threshold. |
98	| Bot-management challenge fires | The route presents the challenge before forwarding to MuleSoft. |
99	
100	## 9. Security and privacy
101	
102	- Card number and PIN are submitted in the POST body only — never as a URL query string. Query strings appear in MRT access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
103	- No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookie may hold the full card number or PIN. Form state lives in React only and is cleared on unmount.
104	- No `console.log`, Sentry breadcrumb, GTM dataLayer push, or analytics event may contain the card number or PIN. The logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must include a redaction rule for this route. No body-logging middleware on the balance-check route.
105	- After submission, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). MuleSoft strips the prefix and check digit before the response reaches MRT.
106	- The MRT balance-check route applies WAF, bot management, rate-limit, and CAPTCHA, because the underlying MuleSoft credential is merchant-level rather than per-shopper. There is no per-customer cap (GC-062); per-IP and per-session limits are enforced at the edge.
107	
108	## 10. Gift card purchase (PWA surface)
109	
110	The storefront sells gift cards as products. The PWA renders the PDP, denomination selector, and gift-details form, and persists gift metadata on the basket. GiveX issuance is server-side after payment capture — the PWA makes no GiveX call on this path.
111	
112	**Scope (confirmed):**
113	- Purchase — domestic storefronts only at launch; international purchase is a future roadmap item.
114	- Redemption (using a gift card as payment) — domestic storefronts only; not at Global-e international checkout at launch (GC-050).
115	- Balance check — all storefronts (GC-059).
116	
117	**Two products:** Physical and digital gift cards are separate SFCC product IDs. Physical cards ship; digital cards send an email to the recipient.
118	
119	**Fixed denominations:** $100, $200, $250, $300, $500. Selected via a searchable dropdown (GC-001–004). The PWA renders the selector from SCAPI product data — the set can change without a code change.
120	
121	**Gift details captured at add-to-cart:** sender name, recipient name, recipient email, delivery date, optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003). The PWA validates recipient email format, delivery date within 3 months, and personal-message length (GC-005–007).
122	
123	**Data flow:** Gift metadata is attached to the basket line item as custom attributes via SCAPI. The PWA persists the metadata and does not call GiveX.
124	
125	**PII:** Recipient name and email are third-party personal data. Carried over HTTPS, not logged beyond SFCC requirements, and subject to the standard data-handling posture.
126	
127	## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation

129	1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** MuleSoft to publish the request and response schema for the balance-check endpoint (including the card number and PIN fields), the error taxonomy mapping GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, and the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the call cannot be implemented against a real MuleSoft instance.
130	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route.
131	3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request. If yes, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

1	# 06 — Booxi (PWA-direct appointment history via MRT proxy)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Booxi is the system of record for boutique appointment data (CRM-166 — the requirement sheet originally referenced "Booksy"; this was a typo, Booxi is the correct vendor). Customer appointment history surfaces within My Account, read directly from the Booxi API by the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`. This is a **PWA-direct path** — it does **not** transit SFCC or MuleSoft.
6	
7	The requirement covers appointment history display only (CRM-165–167); storefront scope and timeline are still TBC. CRM-167 requires the My Account appointments section to be structured so it can be incorporated without structural redesign when Booxi is ready. This document describes the integration shape so the section can be slotted in later without rework; the precise contract is finalised once Booxi confirms its API (see §11).
8	
9	In scope of this document:
10	
11	- Appointment history list rendered inside My Account, read PWA → MRT → Booxi (CRM-165)
12	- The MRT proxy leg that holds the Booxi credential and identifies the customer to Booxi
13	- Embedding, loading, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- Appointment **creation, rescheduling, and cancellation** — not in the current PWA scope. Booking is handled in Booxi's own surfaces; the storefront reads history only. If in-storefront booking is later confirmed, it is added here as a separate write path.
18	- Any SFCC or MuleSoft involvement — there is none on this path.
19	
20	## 2. Vendor relationship
21	
22	- **Vendor:** Booxi — appointment scheduling platform; system of record for Zimmermann boutique appointment data (CRM-166).
23	- **PWA's relationship:** Booxi is consumed read-only. The API contract is owned by Booxi / the Zimmermann CRM team; the PWA team is not a co-developer of the API.
24	
25	## 3. Browser-side architecture
26	
27	The flow below is the recommended design. It is not yet a fixed contract — the customer-identification mechanism is pending confirmation with Booxi (see §11), and the specifics below would change if another scheme is agreed.
28	
29	```
30	Browser (My Account → Appointments section)
31	        │  Customer's SLAS access token (JWT) is present after SFCC login
32	        ▼
33	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/booxi/<endpoint>
34	   Authorization: Bearer <SLAS access token>
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	MRT Node layer:
38	   1. Validates the SLAS JWT signature against SFCC's published JWKS
39	   2. Drops the inbound Authorization header and sets the Booxi credential
40	      header instead (Booxi authenticates via its own `Booxi-PartnerKey`
41	      header, not a bearer `Authorization` header)
42	   3. Resolves the customer's Booxi identity (see §4) and scopes the request to it
43	   4. Forwards to https://<booxi-host>/<endpoint>
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	Booxi API:
47	   • Authorises the request via the Booxi API credential
48	   • Returns the customer's appointment history
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Booxi response → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields the section needs)
52	```
53	
54	- The browser never carries the Booxi credential. The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and is appended only on the MRT → Booxi leg.
55	- The appointments section is read-only and authenticated — it renders only for a logged-in customer on the My Account route.
56	- The section is built as a self-contained module so it can be enabled when Booxi is ready without restructuring the surrounding My Account page (CRM-167).
57	
58	## 4. Authentication and credentials
59	
60	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Booxi Partner API key (sent in the `Booxi-PartnerKey` header) | MRT environment variable; injected by MRT before forwarding | Secret — Booxi mandates this key is used server-side only and never reaches the browser |
63	| Customer SLAS access token (JWT) | Forwarded from the browser to MRT; used by MRT to authenticate the customer | Sensitive — proves user identity |
64	| SFCC JWKS | Used by MRT to verify the SLAS JWT signature | Public |
65	
66	- **No Booxi credential in the browser bundle.** The Booxi credential is held server-side as an MRT environment variable, appended on the MRT → Booxi leg only.
67	- **Customer identification (open — see §11).** The PWA must prove *which* customer's appointments to return without letting the browser request an arbitrary customer's data. The recommended approach is that MRT validates the customer's SLAS JWT and resolves the corresponding Booxi customer reference server-side (from a Booxi customer ID held on the SFCC/Omneo profile, or via a Booxi lookup), then scopes the request to that reference. MRT must never accept a raw Booxi customer ID, email, or appointment ID from the browser as the identity input.
68	- One Booxi API credential per environment. Rotation cadence and named owner are tracked in §11.
69	
70	## 5. Data exchanged
71	
72	| Direction | Data | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| Browser → MRT | Customer JWT (SLAS access token); endpoint path | The browser never sees the Booxi credential and never passes a customer identifier as input. |
75	| MRT → Booxi | Booxi API credential; customer-scoped identifier resolved server-side | The credential authorises the channel; the resolved identity scopes the data. |
76	| Booxi → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — appointment history (date/time, boutique, appointment type, status) | MRT projects only the fields the My Account section renders. |
77	
78	The customer sees only their own appointment data, which they already own. No payment data is involved on this path.
79	
80	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
81	
82	- The appointment history read fires only when the My Account appointments section is in view — it does not preload on the dashboard or any other route.
83	- TanStack Query caches the appointment history response on the client; stale data is acceptable for history display.
84	- The My Account appointments module is route-level code-split so it adds nothing to other route bundles, and so it can ship dark until Booxi is enabled (CRM-167).
85	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Booxi host is emitted from the My Account routes once the customer is authenticated and the section is enabled.
86	
87	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
88	
89	- Appointments are boutique-bound; the history list reflects whichever boutiques the customer has booked with, independent of the storefront locale.
90	- A single Booxi tenant is assumed across all eight storefronts; per-region boutique availability is configured in Booxi, not in the PWA.
91	- Locale affects only the display formatting of dates and labels in the storefront, not the Booxi request.
92	
93	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
94	
95	Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.
96	
97	| Failure | Behaviour |
98	|---|---|
99	| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
100	| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
101	| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
102	| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
103	| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |
104	
105	## 9. Security and privacy
106	
107	- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
108	- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
109	- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
110	- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
111	- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.
112	
113	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
114	
115	1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
116	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
117	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
118	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.
