1	# 07 — Adyen (Payments)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Adyen is the payment service provider for **all SFCC-owned (domestic) checkout** on Zimmermann storefronts: AU, US (when shipping to the US), UK, and EU domestic. International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US shipping internationally) is owned by Global-e and does not involve Adyen at the PWA layer.
6	
7	The PWA loads the Adyen Web Drop-in at the payment step of checkout. Card details are tokenised inside an Adyen-hosted iframe — they never reach Zimmermann or SFCC infrastructure.
8	
9	In scope for this document:
10	
11	- Adyen Web Drop-in initialisation, configuration, and rendering
12	- Card tokenisation inside the Adyen-hosted iframe
13	- 3D Secure 2 inline challenge (no redirect off checkout)
14	- Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna where supported (launch and August 2026 wave)
15	- Saved-card display (brand, last four, expiry) via Adyen token references stored in SFCC
16	- RevenueProtect risk signals collected client-side (device fingerprint, browser metadata)
17	
18	Server-side payment calls (`/payments`, capture, refund, void), webhooks from Adyen, and Adyen Customer Area configuration are all handled by the SFCC cartridge — no PWA involvement.
19	
20	## 2. Vendor relationship
21	
22	- **Vendor:** Adyen N.V.
23	- **Payment methods in scope:** Web Drop-in, 3DS2, RevenueProtect, Tokenisation, Pay by Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna where applicable.
24	- **Adyen Web SDK version:** Adyen Web v6 (current stable major) at implementation start, pinned in the bundle, upgraded on a quarterly cadence. v6 instantiates the Drop-in via an async constructor (`const checkout = await AdyenCheckout({...})`) — the v5-era `AdyenCheckout.create()` factory was removed in v6 — requires Adyen Checkout API v69 or later, makes `countryCode` a required initialisation property per the v5→v6 migration guide (the Sessions flow supplies it automatically from the session payload), and uses CSS custom properties for styling.
25	
26	## 3. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	Checkout — payment step entered
30	        │
31	        ▼
32	PWA calls SFCC:  POST /sessions  (SFCC calls Adyen /sessions on
33	                                   behalf of the PWA — Adyen's modern flow)
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	SFCC returns the Adyen session ({ id, sessionData } plus
37	                                  amount, countryCode, returnUrl, expiresAt)
38	                                  alongside the public client key and
39	                                  environment (SFCC-configured values)
40	        │
41	        ▼
42	PWA dynamically imports the Adyen Web Drop-in bundle on payment step entry
43	        │
44	        ▼
45	Drop-in renders inside an Adyen-hosted iframe for cards (PCI scope reduction)
46	and as a native button for Apple Pay / Google Pay
47	        │
48	        ▼
49	User submits — Drop-in handles tokenisation, 3DS2 inline, and the redirect
50	flow for PayPal / Klarna entirely from the session.
51	        │
52	        ▼
53	Drop-in calls the merchant return URL on success → SFCC reconciles → PWA
54	shows the order-confirmation page.
55	```
56	
57	- The Adyen Sessions flow is used. One server-side `/sessions` call from SFCC creates a payment session; the Drop-in handles everything thereafter — including 3DS2 inline rendering, PayPal / Klarna redirects, and final result reporting — without further `/payments` calls from the PWA.
58	- The Adyen bundle is loaded only when the customer enters the payment step. It is not in the global bundle and does not load on PDP, cart, or the delivery / address step.
59	- 3DS2 challenge is always inline (the SDK's native 3DS2 flow). The shopper does not leave the checkout page (PAY-045).
60	- For PayPal and Klarna the shopper is redirected off-site and returned via the configured return URL; on return, the billing address is pre-populated from the redirect payload (PAY-003, PAY-023 cover PayPal).
61	- The Drop-in for cards renders inside an Adyen-hosted iframe, so the PWA bundle never touches PAN, CVV, or cardholder name.
62	- When paying with a previously saved card, the PWA requires the customer to re-enter the card's CVV/CVC at the point of payment (PAY-022). The CVV/CVC field is captured inside the Adyen Drop-in's stored-card flow; the value lives in React state only, is never logged or persisted client-side, and is cleared on submit/unmount — see §8. The 3DS re-challenge decision is owned by Adyen (outside the PWA boundary); the PWA does not control whether 3DS re-prompts.
63	- A second CVC prompt is triggered at the **address step** when a returning customer with a saved card enters a new/unsaved shipping address (Adyen-confirmed 2026-06-25 — see §8 for full detail and the two-part build required).
64	
65	## 4. Authentication and credentials
66	
67	The Adyen client key is public and embedded in the Drop-in init. It is bound to an Adyen API credential (web-service user) that is origin-restricted per environment in the Adyen Customer Area. All server-side credentials (API key, HMAC secret) live in the SFCC cartridge — the PWA never holds or sees them.
68	
69	## 5. Data exchanged (browser ↔ Adyen)
70	
71	| Direction | Data | Notes |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| PWA → Drop-in | Adyen session reference from SFCC (`id` + opaque `sessionData`, plus amount, currency, countryCode, return URL), and the public client key, environment, and shopper locale set in the Drop-in config | `sessionData` is opaque and passes through the PWA; the client key and environment are client-side config, not part of the Adyen `/sessions` response |
74	| Drop-in → Adyen | Card PAN, expiry, CVV, cardholder name (encrypted inside the iframe); device fingerprint and browser metadata for 3DS2 | Inside the Adyen iframe — never visible to PWA JavaScript |
75	| Adyen → Drop-in → PWA | Tokenised payment method blob; 3DS challenge data; final result code | The blob is opaque to the PWA and is forwarded verbatim to SFCC |
76	
77	For a saved card, the customer-entered CVV/CVC (PAY-022) is captured inside the Adyen iframe and never visible to PWA JavaScript. It is held in React state only for the duration of the payment step, never logged (no `console.*`, Sentry, GTM/dataLayer, or MRT access log) and never persisted client-side (no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookies); it is cleared on submit/unmount and is sent only in the POST body, never as a query string. See §8.
78	
79	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
80	
81	- The Adyen Web Drop-in bundle (in the low-hundred-KB-gzip range for a card + wallets configuration) is dynamically imported on payment-step entry. It does not contribute to LCP on the homepage, PLP, PDP, cart, or address page.
82	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the live Adyen Checkout API host is emitted from the cart step so the TLS handshake is warm by the time the customer reaches payment.
83	- The 3DS2 inline challenge iframe is sized in advance to avoid layout shift on render.
84	
85	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
86	
87	| Region | Currency | Launch methods | August 2026 additions |
88	|---|---|---|---|
89	| AU | AUD | Card (Visa, MC, Amex), PayPal | Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna |
90	| US | USD | Card, PayPal | Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna |
91	| UK | GBP | Card, PayPal | Apple Pay, Google Pay |
92	| EU domestic | EUR | Card, PayPal, plus locally enabled methods | Apple Pay, Google Pay |
93	
94	- **Klarna is AU and US only (PAY-007).** It is not in scope for UK or EU domestic at launch.
95	- The Drop-in receives the available methods list dynamically from the session payload — the storefront does not hard-code methods per region.
96	- Tax labels for receipts (GST for AU, VAT for UK and EU, Tax for US) are passed alongside the order for Adyen reporting (PAY-063).
97	
98	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
99	
100	| Failure | Behaviour |
101	|---|---|
102	| Adyen Drop-in bundle fails to load | Show an error on the payment step with a "Reload" CTA. Block order placement. Log to monitoring. |
103	| Drop-in initialises but submission fails (network) | Adyen surfaces the inline error inside the iframe; the shopper can retry. No retry cap is enforced by the storefront (PAY-014). |
104	| Auth refused (`Refused`, `Declined`, `Cancelled`) | Friendly message ("Payment was declined — please try a different payment method"). The raw reason code is never shown to the shopper. |
105	| 3DS2 challenge timeout / failure | Treated as refused; the shopper can re-attempt. |
106	| Apple Pay or Google Pay unavailable on device | The button is hidden. The card path remains. |
107	| RevenueProtect places order in fraud review (e-gift card orders, per PAY-044) | The order is accepted but fulfilment and e-gift card code delivery are withheld until operations resolve. The confirmation page shows "Order confirmed — additional review in progress". |
108	| Adyen API or Customer Area outage | Existing Drop-in sessions already issued continue. New session creation fails — treated as a P1 incident. |
109	
110	## 9. Security and privacy
111	
112	- The Adyen client key is public and constrained by the allowed-origins list on its Adyen API credential (one origin per environment).
113	- All card data is captured inside the Adyen-hosted iframe; the PWA bundle and SFCC see only opaque token references. The use of the Adyen-hosted iframe approach is what makes SAQ-A PCI scope viable (TBC — formal scope confirmation with Adyen during onboarding).
114	- 3DS2 is mandatory for cards in the UK and EU per regulation and is enabled for AU and US per risk policy.
115	- Saved cards (PAY-017 – PAY-021) are opt-in only ("Save this card to your account for faster checkout", unchecked by default). The display in My Account shows brand, last four, and expiry — sourced from Adyen via the token reference. Removal in My Account deletes the corresponding token in Adyen.
116	- **Saved-card CVV re-entry (PAY-022).** When a customer pays with a previously saved card, the PWA requires them to re-enter the card's CVV/CVC at the point of payment before the order can be placed. The value is captured inside the Adyen Drop-in's stored-card flow and is handled as a payment credential: it is **never logged** (no `console.*`, Sentry, GTM/dataLayer, or MRT access log), **never persisted client-side** (no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookies), lives in **React state only**, is **cleared on submit/unmount**, and is sent **only in the POST body** (never as a query string). The **3DS re-challenge decision is owned by Adyen** (outside the PWA boundary) — the PWA does not control whether 3DS re-prompts.
117	  - *Note:* the enhancement ENH-019 (CVV-on-saved-cards) is **Cancelled — folded into the confirmed PAY-022 requirement** above. The only residual is the **Adyen-side CVC-on-saved-card configuration**, pending Adyen confirmation (an Adyen-team dependency, not a PWA-build blocker).
118	- **CVC re-entry on new shipping address (Adyen-confirmed 2026-06-25 — do not overwrite without re-confirming with Adyen).** When a returning customer selects a saved card and enters a new/unsaved shipping address during checkout, the PWA must display a CVC input field at the address step before the customer can proceed to payment. This is a two-part build confirmed by Adyen on 2026-06-25:
119	  1. **SFCC PWA frontend** — the PWA detects the condition (saved card selected + new/unsaved shipping address entered) and mounts an Adyen Secured Fields CVC component at the address step. Adyen cannot inject this UI dynamically; the field must come from the frontend. The component must be iframe-backed (Adyen Secured Fields, not a raw HTML `<input>`) to preserve PCI SAQ-A scope. Note: loading the Secured Fields SDK at the address step is earlier than the current payment-step-only load strategy (§6); assess impact against the LCP budget before implementation.
120	  2. **Adyen backend** — a Custom Risk Rule is configured in the Adyen Customer Area to verify that CVC was provided and matched for transactions where a new shipping address was used. If the rule is not satisfied, Adyen blocks the transaction or routes it to manual review. Configuration of this rule is an Adyen-side item (see open item #3), not a PWA build blocker, but it is a hard dependency for the fraud logic to function.
121	
122	  The same security handling as PAY-022 applies: the CVC value is never logged, never persisted client-side, lives in React state only, and is cleared on proceed/unmount. *A corresponding PRD requirement is pending a new requirement ID from the client; a traceability note has been added to checkout.md PAY-022 in the interim.*
123	- Cards saved via Global-e international checkouts are not synced back to SFCC or Adyen (CRM-173) and never appear in the storefront-managed saved-card list.
124	
125	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
126	
127	1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
128	2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.

1	# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.
6	
7	PWA responsibilities:
8	
9	- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
10	- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
11	- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
12	- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
13	- Handling the order-completion return path
14	
15	Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.
16	
17	## 2. Checkout ownership matrix
18	
19	| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
20	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
21	| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
22	| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
23	| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
24	| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
25	| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
26	| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
27	| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
28	| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |
29	
30	Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.
31	
32	> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.
33	
34	## 3. Browser-side architecture
35	
36	```
37	Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
38	        │
39	        ▼
40	PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
41	price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
42	        │
43	        ▼
44	Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
45	        │
46	        ▼
47	Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
48	shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
52	`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
53	`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
54	        │
55	        ▼
56	PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
57	inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
58	(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
59	        │
60	        ▼
61	Inside the iframe Global-e collects shipping address, payment, duties, and tax.
62	When the shopper clicks "Place Order", Global-e calls the SFCC
63	`Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
64	If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to cart —
65	no order is created on either side.
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	After validation passes, Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame.
69	The parent frame makes an AJAX request to SFCC `orderCreate()`, which converts
70	the basket to an SFCC order with status **Created**. If this call fails (session
71	expiry, stock change) Global-e's retry mechanism falls back to the
72	`SendOrderToMerchant` path to recreate and place the order.
73	        │
74	        ▼
75	Global-e calls SFCC's `SendOrderToMerchant` endpoint seconds later to enrich
76	the order with full international transaction data. Order status → **New**.
77	        │
78	        ▼
79	After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC's `PerformPayment` endpoint.
80	Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
81	        │
82	        ▼
83	Order completion: the PWA navigates the parent frame to the Zimmermann
84	confirmation route, fetches the order from SFCC, and renders the confirmation.
85	The order number shown to shoppers is the Global-e order number
86	(format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`); SFCC domestic orders
87	continue to show the SFCC order number.
88	```
89	
90	- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.
91	  SFCC holds these price books, regenerated nightly from Global-e's FX, coefficient, and rounding feed (PRC-34, PRC-38..40).
92	  Calculated prices are also in the SFCC search index so price filters and sort work on PLP and search results (PRC-41).
93	  The PWA does not convert prices client-side — it formats the SFCC-supplied target-currency price per locale (symbol position, decimal places including zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator) per PRC-47.
94	  HK and ME follow the same pattern: prices are read from HKD and AED SFCC price books, not from a Global-e client-side widget.
95	  No Global-e client-side script is needed to display pricing.
96	
97	- **DDP/DDU duties messaging.** Shown on PDP per destination country, configurable per country (PRC-15). The data source for this flag (SFCC product attribute vs. Global-e price book field) is not specified in the PRDs — confirm with the integration team before implementing.
98	
99	- **Handoff payload.** SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency at handoff — line items, quantities, target-currency prices, applied promotions, coupons, Retail Rewards, and gift cards (PRC-16).
100	  Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards.
101	
102	- **Iframe embed.** The Global-e checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route. The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive must list the Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1). Iframe height is managed via Global-e's `postMessage` contract.
103	
104	- **Shipping country lock.** The shipping country is determined by the country selector pre-checkout and cannot be changed inside the Global-e iframe (REG-028).
105	
106	- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
107	  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
108	  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
109	  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
110	  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
111	  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
112	  After all three checks pass:
113	  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
114	  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.
115	  - Navigate the parent frame to `/{prefix}/checkout/confirmation?<encoded-params>` and render the confirmation from the SFCC order record.
116	  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).
117	
118	## 4. Authentication and credentials
119	
120	| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
121	| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
122	| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
123	| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
124	
125	## 5. Data exchanged
126	
127	**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**
128	
129	- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
130	- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
131	- Order reference for return-webhook correlation
132	
133	**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**
134	
135	- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
136	- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
137	- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
138	- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
139	- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)
140	
141	**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.
142	
143	**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**
144	
145	Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
146	The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.
147	
148	| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
149	| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
150	| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
151	| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
152	| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
153	| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |
154	
155	Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
156	`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
157	Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.
158	
159	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
160	
161	- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
162	- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.
163	- Emit `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Global-e checkout origin from the cart page to warm the TLS handshake before the iframe loads.
164	- Any retained Global-e client-side script (e.g. duties messaging) must be deferred and load after LCP.
165	- The Global-e team must configure `frame-ancestors` / `X-Frame-Options` to permit embedding under `www.zimmermann.com`.
166	
167	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
168	
169	| Failure                                                                    | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
170	| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
171	| SFCC Global-e-derived price book is missing or stale for a target currency | Show the storefront-currency price with the message "Final pricing in your currency shown at checkout." Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk. |
172	| Handoff fails (Global-e API outage at cart → handoff)                      | Surface a hard error: "International checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." Do not place the order in SFCC.                                                                                                                                                   |
173	| Return webhook from Global-e to SFCC is delayed                            | Render the confirmation with the order reference and a "Your order is being processed" state. Full details render once SFCC receives the order.                                                                                                                                        |
174	| Cart total mismatch between SFCC and Global-e at handoff                   | Reject the order; surface a hard error. Never silently adjust totals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
175	
176	## 8. Security
177	
178	- The Global-e checkout domain is third-party. Cross-site cookies do not propagate — cart context is passed inside the handoff payload, not via cookies.
179	- The `postMessage` listener in the parent frame must enforce all three checks documented in §3 — `event.origin`, `event.source`, and message schema — plus `orderRef` format validation and URL-safe query encoding before constructing the confirmation URL. See §3 "Return path" for the full requirements.
180	
181	## 9. Open items
182	
183	1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply:
184	
185	   - The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers.
186	   - The `postMessage` trusted sender origin — the vendor guide confirms that the Global-e iframe sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame to trigger `orderCreate()`, but does not specify the exact origin string or the full message schema. The `event.origin` value and message payload shape must be obtained from Global-e directly before the listener can be safely implemented.
187	     Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.
188	
189	2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order (from SFCC), to decide between full order detail and a "View on tracking page" fallback.
190	   Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

1	# 09 — Google Maps Platform (Address Autocomplete)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google Maps Platform — specifically the Places API (Autocomplete) — provides address autocomplete at checkout for both delivery and billing addresses (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059), and in the Address Book (My Account) for saved-address creation (CRM-053), replacing the legacy Loqate / PCA Predict integration used on Magento.
6	
7	In-scope surfaces:
8	
9	- **Checkout — address step** (delivery and billing).
10	- **Address Book (My Account)** — address creation reuses the same Places integration for validation and autocomplete, with the customer still able to opt into the full manual form (CRM-053, Confirmed).
11	
12	In scope:
13	
14	- Autocomplete predictions as the shopper types
15	- Place Details retrieval for the structured address components of the selected prediction
16	- Session tokens to optimise per-session billing
17	- Always-available fallback to manual address entry, on every in-scope surface
18	
19	Out of scope:
20	
21	- BOPIS boutique-selector map (CFD-034) — separate Google Maps JavaScript usage
22	- Directions, Distance Matrix, Geocoding, Routes API
23	- Store locator — consumes the Google Business feed loaded into SFCC, not the Places API
24	
25	## 2. PWA-layer architecture
26	
27	The browser never calls Google directly. All Places API calls are proxied through the Managed Runtime Node layer, which holds the API key as an environment variable and injects it on outbound requests.
28	
29	```
30	Checkout — address step (delivery or billing)
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	Shopper focuses the address field
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	PWA generates a fresh session token (client-side UUID v4)
37	        │
38	        ├──► On keystroke (debounced 200 ms):
39	        │         Browser  POST /mobify/proxy/google/v1/places:autocomplete
40	        │                  body: { input, sessionToken,
41	        │                          includedRegionCodes: [...],
42	        │                          languageCode }
43	        │         MRT      injects the API key as the X-Goog-Api-Key header,
44	        │                  forwards to
45	        │                  places.googleapis.com/v1/places:autocomplete
46	        │         Returns  prediction list
47	        │
48	        ├──► On prediction select:
49	        │         Browser  GET /mobify/proxy/google/v1/places/{place_id}
50	        │                  ?sessionToken={sessionToken}
51	        │                  header: X-Goog-FieldMask: addressComponents,
52	        │                          formattedAddress, location
53	        │         MRT      injects the API key, forwards to
54	        │                  places.googleapis.com/v1/places/{place_id}
55	        │         Returns  structured address components
56	        │
57	        └──► Map address components → SFCC address fields (line1, line2,
58	              city, state, postal code, country). Discard the session token.
59	```
60	
61	- **No Google Maps JavaScript SDK is loaded for address autocomplete.** All autocomplete calls are lightweight `fetch` requests to the MRT proxy. No `<script>` tag, no SDK loader, no third-party impact on bundle size or LCP. (The separate BOPIS boutique-selector map per CFD-034 does use the Maps JavaScript API; it is out of scope here.)
62	- **Session tokens** are client-generated UUIDs sent on both the Autocomplete and the Place Details call. Per Google's Places API (New) pricing, session-bundled requests are cheaper.
63	- **Region scoping.** `includedRegionCodes` is set per active storefront (see §8) to narrow predictions and reduce noise and cost.
64	- **Field projection.** Place Details responses are limited to `addressComponents`, `formattedAddress`, and `location` via the `X-Goog-FieldMask` header — keeps payload and cost low.
65	- **Manual entry is always available.** An "Enter address manually" link below the autocomplete field reveals the discrete address fields. This is the always-on fallback on every in-scope surface.
66	- **The same flow serves both surfaces.** The Address Book (My Account) saved-address creation form reuses this exact autocomplete-and-validate flow and the same MRT proxy (CRM-053), so the proxy path, session-token handling, field projection, and manual-form fallback above apply identically there. The only difference from checkout is the mount point; no separate integration is built.
67	
68	## 3. Authentication and credentials
69	
70	| Credential | Where held | Sensitivity |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| Maps API key | MRT environment variable; injected server-side by the proxy on outbound requests | Secret — must not be bundled into browser JavaScript or logged (it travels in the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header on the MRT→Google leg) |
73	
74	
75	## 4. Data exchanged
76	
77	| Direction | Data | Notes |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Browser → MRT proxy | Partial address string, session token, included region codes, language code | API key is not sent by the browser — MRT injects it. |
80	| MRT → Google | Same payload plus the API key header | Forwarded server-side to `places.googleapis.com`. |
81	| Google → MRT → Browser | Prediction list (suggestion text, place ID, structured components) | Field-masked. |
82	| Browser → MRT (details) | Selected place ID, session token, field mask | Field projection keeps the response small. |
83	| Google → MRT → Browser (details) | Address components, formatted address, latitude / longitude | Lat/lng is captured for any distance / proximity logic but is not stored beyond the address form's lifetime. |
84	
85	The PWA never sends the shopper's name, email, or any other identifier to Google. The address fragment is the only personal data leaving the browser, and only the partial value the shopper has typed.
86	
87	## 5. Performance and loading strategy
88	
89	- No third-party script load — there is no LCP impact and no bundle size cost beyond the storefront's own autocomplete component.
90	- A 500 ms debounce on keystrokes keeps request volume and cost reasonable.
91	- Field projection on Place Details keeps payload small.
92	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Google host is not emitted because the browser never connects to Google directly.
93	
94	## 6. Multi-region behaviour
95	
96	`includedRegionCodes` is set per active storefront to mirror the country-to-storefront routing:
97	
98	| Storefront | Included region codes |
99	|---|---|
100	| AU | AU plus Oceania (NZ, FJ, NC, …) |
101	| US (`/us/`) | US, PR |
102	| US international (`/en-ca/`) | All Americas excluding US (pre-handoff capture; Global-e takes over inside its iframe) |
103	| UK | GB |
104	| EU domestic | DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, BE, … (the full EU domestic list) |
105	| EU international | Non-EU Europe plus Africa long tail (pre-handoff) |
106	| HK | HK plus the APAC long tail |
107	| ME | UAE plus GCC and Levant |
108	
109	For Global-e-owned storefronts the autocomplete is used on the Zimmermann-side address step where applicable. Inside the Global-e iframe Global-e's own address widget takes over.
110	
111	`includedRegionCodes` accepts at most **15** two-character region codes per request (Places API New). Storefronts whose routing spans more than 15 countries (e.g. EU domestic, the US-international Americas list, the HK APAC long tail) cannot enumerate every country here — cap the list at the 15 highest-traffic codes, or rely on `locationBias` / `locationRestriction` instead of region codes for broader scoping.
112	
113	`languageCode` is set to the active storefront locale so prediction labels render in the shopper's language.
114	
115	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
116	
117	| Failure | Behaviour |
118	|---|---|
119	| MRT proxy unavailable | The storefront falls back to manual address entry immediately. No error toast is shown — the manual form is the natural fallback. |
120	| Places API returns 5xx or quota exceeded | Switch the field to manual entry silently. Log the response code to monitoring. |
121	| Place Details fails after a successful Autocomplete | Pre-fill `line 1` with the prediction's formatted text and surface the remaining fields as manual. The shopper completes the rest. |
122	| Prediction is a valid Google address but not shippable by the storefront | SFCC-side validation rejects on submit with a clear message. The region-scoping in §8 reduces but does not eliminate this case. |
123	| Cost spike (malicious or bot traffic) | GCP budget alerts page the integration team. Short-term mitigation: tighten or remove the field from the address form (manual entry always available). |
124	
125	## 8. Security and privacy
126	
127	- The API key never reaches the browser; it is injected by the MRT proxy. There is no path by which a bundle leak could expose it.
128	- Address fragments the shopper types are forwarded to Google. This is disclosed in the Didomi notice and the Privacy Policy.
129	- No Google JavaScript SDK loads in the browser for the autocomplete integration, so Google sets no cookies via an autocomplete SDK on the Zimmermann origin.
130	
131	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
132	
133	1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
134

1	# 10 — Google reCAPTCHA (Bot Protection)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google reCAPTCHA v3 provides bot protection on the registration and login forms. The PWA loads the reCAPTCHA script in the browser, collects a token when the customer submits the form, and the MRT layer verifies that token with Google before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never leaves the server.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- reCAPTCHA v3 script load on the register and login forms (browser)
10	- Token submission alongside form data to the MRT layer
11	- MRT-side token verification against Google's `siteverify` endpoint
12	- Per-region consent gating (EU and UK only)
13	
14	Out of scope of this document:
15	
16	- reCAPTCHA on the gift-card balance-check route — that is an open question (owned separately by the GiveX integration)
17	- reCAPTCHA Enterprise — v3 is the confirmed version
18	
19	## 2. How it works
20	
21	```
22	Customer fills in register / login form
23	        │  (form interaction — reCAPTCHA script loads here, not on page load)
24	        ▼
25	reCAPTCHA v3 runs silently in the background and returns a token
26	        │
27	        ▼
28	Form submits token + credentials to MRT
29	        │
30	        ▼
31	MRT calls Google siteverify:
32	  POST https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify
33	  Body: secret=RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY&response=<token>
34	        │
35	        ├── score low / token invalid → reject; return error to the browser
36	        └── score acceptable         → forward request to SCAPI
37	```
38	
39	- The reCAPTCHA script is loaded **on form interaction only** (not on page load), so it never sits on the critical path for first paint.
40	- The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable) and is never exposed in the browser bundle, request URLs, or logs.
41	- The site key (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`) is a public identifier, safe to embed in the bundle.
42	
43	## 3. Credentials
44	
45	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Site key (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`) | Browser — initialises the reCAPTCHA script | Public — bound to the registered domain |
48	| Secret key (`RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`) | MRT environment variable — used server-side for `siteverify` verification | Secret — never reaches the browser |
49	
50	One site key / secret key pair per environment.
51	
52	## 4. Consent and gating
53	
54	- **Most regions:** reCAPTCHA loads on register / login form interaction regardless of Didomi consent state — no consent required.
55	- **EU and UK:** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated — it loads only after Didomi consent is granted. A visitor who declines gets no bot protection on those forms. This is a regulatory trade-off, not a technical limitation.
56	
57	## 5. Performance
58	
59	- The reCAPTCHA script is ~100 KB gzipped. Loading it on form interaction (not page load) means it has zero impact on LCP for any browsing page.
60	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `www.google.com/recaptcha` and `www.gstatic.com` can be emitted from the register / login route to warm the connection without affecting earlier pages.
61	
62	## 6. Multi-region behaviour
63	
64	| Region | Consent-gated? | Notes |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| AU | No | Loads on form interaction |
67	| US | No | Loads on form interaction |
68	| UK | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
69	| EU domestic | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
70	| EU international | Yes (EU/UK rule) | Loads only after Didomi consent |
71	| HK | No | Loads on form interaction |
72	| ME | No | Loads on form interaction |
73	
74	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
75	
76	| Failure | Behaviour |
77	|---|---|
78	| reCAPTCHA script fails to load (CDN outage, browser extension) | Block form submission; show a "please try again" message. |
79	| MRT `siteverify` call times out or Google returns an error | Block form submission; show a "please try again" message. Log to monitoring. |
80	| Token score is below the acceptable threshold | Treat as a bot; reject silently with a generic error message (do not tell the user why). |
81	| User in EU / UK declines Didomi consent | No reCAPTCHA loads; form submission proceeds without bot protection. No error shown to the user. |
82	
83	## 8. Security
84	
85	- The secret key is never logged, never embedded in the browser bundle, and never passed as a URL query parameter. It is held as an MRT environment variable and used only in the server-side `siteverify` POST body.
86	- Score thresholds are configured in the MRT verification layer (not in reCAPTCHA itself — v3 has no server-side threshold config). The working threshold is 0.5; adjust based on observed production traffic.
87	
88	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
89	
90	1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only) per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
91	
92	2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK (§4). Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

1	# 11 — Narvar (Estimated Delivery Date Widget)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Narvar provides the pre-purchase and post-purchase delivery experience for SFCC-owned domestic orders. The PWA loads Narvar's pre-purchase widget — **Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT)** — at the checkout delivery-method step to display an Estimated Delivery Date alongside each method (DLV-009, CFD-050). (The technical bundle/API identifiers below retain the "convert" name.)
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) widget initialisation on the checkout delivery-method step
10	- EDD display per delivery method (a range such as "2–4 business days, delivered by Fri 12 Jun")
11	- Suppression of the EDD line when the widget cannot resolve a date or fails to load
12	
13	Out of scope of this document (server-side via SFCC → MuleSoft → Narvar, or out-of-band):
14	
15	- Domestic order confirmation emails (Narvar Notify — triggered from SFCC at order placement, CFD-069)
16	- Shipping confirmation emails (Narvar Notify)
17	- Tracking portal on a Zimmermann-branded subdomain (Narvar-hosted; exact host TBC, linked from emails and My Account)
18	- Returns portal (Narvar Concierge), entered from My Account using billing email plus order number (RRC-005). Narvar owns only the returns *initiation* portal; return history and status shown in My Account are sourced from NewStore via MuleSoft — not from Narvar (RRC-007, RRC-008, RRC-014).
19	- International orders — Narvar is not used for international destinations; Global-e owns international fulfilment messaging
20	
21	## 2. Browser-side architecture
22	
23	```
24	Checkout — delivery method step entered
25	        │
26	        ▼
27	PWA dynamically loads the Narvar CONVERT bundle
28	(deferred behind Didomi Performance consent)
29	        │
30	        ▼
31	PWA calls the CONVERT API with:
32	   retailer ID, shipping postcode, country, line items (SKU, quantity),
33	   order timestamp, available delivery method codes
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	Narvar returns an EDD object per method:
37	   { method: "express", earliestDate, latestDate, businessDays }
38	        │
39	        ▼
40	PWA renders the EDD inline beside each delivery method (CFD-049, CFD-050)
41	```
42	
43	- The CONVERT bundle loads only on the delivery-method step — not on PDP, cart, or any earlier page.
44	- The widget is asynchronous. Delivery methods and costs render immediately from SFCC; the EDD line appears as soon as Narvar responds. Working defaults: 500 ms target, 2-second hard timeout (see §7).
45	- Single delivery method is presented at checkout per DLV-014 — if NewStore later splits the order into multiple shipments, that is communicated post-purchase through Narvar tracking, not at checkout.
46	
47	## 3. Credentials
48	
49	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
50	|---|---|---|
51	| Narvar retailer ID | Embedded in the CONVERT bundle URL | Public |
52	| CONVERT API key | Embedded client-side; domain-restricted | Public-scoped |
53	
54	One account serves all domestic regions — the retailer ID and CONVERT API key are the same across AU, US, UK, and EU domestic.
55	
56	## 4. Data exchanged
57	
58	| Direction | Data | Notes |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| Browser → Narvar | Postcode, country, line items (SKU, quantity), available delivery method codes, order timestamp | No PII — no name, no email, no street address. For multi-quantity line items, pass unit tax value divided by quantity, not the total line tax (PAY-064). |
61	| Narvar → Browser | EDD range per delivery method | Strings formatted by the storefront for locale. |
62	
63	Per CFD-050 the full street address is not passed to the CONVERT widget — postcode and country are sufficient and minimise PII exposure.
64	
65	## 5. Consent and gating
66	
67	- Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) is loaded under the Performance Didomi consent category (TBC — REG-051 defines the category set; assignment to Performance is a working assumption pending Zimmermann confirmation).
68	- EDD improves the experience but checkout completes without it.
69	- If Performance consent is denied the widget does not load. The storefront shows shipping method names and costs without an EDD line.
70	
71	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
72	
73	- The CONVERT bundle is small (approximately 30 KB gzip — vendor-stated; confirm at integration time). It is loaded with `async` and deferred to the delivery-method step.
74	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Narvar CDN origin is emitted from the cart page so the TLS handshake is warm by the time the widget loads.
75	- The storefront does not block delivery-method rendering on Narvar. The EDD line is a progressive enhancement on top of the SFCC-supplied methods and costs.
76	
77	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
78	
79	| Region | EDD source |
80	|---|---|
81	| AU including Oceania domestic | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) |
82	| US domestic | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) |
83	| UK | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) |
84	| EU domestic (FR, IT, ES, DE, …) | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) |
85	| US international (`/en-ca/`) | Global-e (Narvar not used) |
86	| EU international (`/en-ch/`) | Global-e (Narvar not used) |
87	| HK | Global-e (Narvar not used) |
88	| ME | Global-e (Narvar not used) |
89	
90	The CONVERT request carries the storefront locale and date-format hints so the returned strings render correctly per region.
91	
92	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
93	
94	| Failure | Behaviour |
95	|---|---|
96	| CONVERT script fails to load | Suppress the EDD line. Shipping methods and costs continue to render. Checkout is not blocked. Logged to monitoring. |
97	| CONVERT API 5xx or timeout above 2 seconds | Suppress the EDD line for the affected method. Other methods continue if they respond. |
98	| CONVERT returns an obviously wrong date (past, or more than 60 days out) | Storefront-side sanity check rejects the value and suppresses the line. Logged. (60-day ceiling is a working default.) |
99	| Postcode unrecognised by Narvar | Suppress the EDD line for that destination. Do not block submission. |
100	
101	The graceful policy is that the EDD widget must never block checkout — the order placement path does not depend on Narvar.
102	
103	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
104	
105	1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.
106	
107	2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.
108

1	# 12 — Didomi (Consent Management Platform)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Didomi is the Consent Management Platform (CMP) for all seven Zimmermann storefronts. It is the gatekeeper for every third-party script that loads in the browser — marketing tags, analytics tags, heatmap and session-replay tools, the live-chat widget, the Adyen Drop-in, the Narvar EDD widget, and Google reCAPTCHA all wait on a Didomi signal before initialising.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- First-load cookie banner and consent UI
10	- Persistence of consent choices across sessions and pages
11	- Re-prompt and preference-centre access
12	- Consent callbacks consumed by application code to gate downstream scripts
13	- Google Consent Mode v2 signal emission (`ad_storage`, `ad_user_data`, `ad_personalization`, `analytics_storage`)
14	
15	Out of scope of this document:
16	
17	- The downstream tags themselves — owned by Tell No Lies inside the GTM container
18	- Server-side consent recording or back-office reporting
19	
20	## 2. Browser-side architecture
21	
22	```
23	First page load
24	        │
25	        ▼
26	@didomi/react component mounted at the top of the React tree
27	   (which injects Didomi loader from sdk.privacy-center.org)
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	Didomi SDK initialises ─────► reads persisted consent (cookie + localStorage)
31	        │
32	        ├── consent already given → fires consent.changed immediately
33	        │           │
34	        │           ▼
35	        │     App listeners load gated scripts (GTM, Inside Chat,
36	        │     Narvar EDD widget, Adyen, reCAPTCHA, etc.)
37	        │
38	        └── no prior consent → Didomi renders the banner
39	                    │
40	                    ▼
41	                User makes a choice
42	                    │
43	                    ▼
44	                consent.changed event fires with the new purpose and vendor IDs
45	```
46	
47	- The PWA uses the **`@didomi/react`** package to mount the SDK as early as possible at the top of the React tree. This is the Didomi-recommended approach for SPAs and keeps configuration tied to a single component rather than a raw script tag.
48	- The SDK's loader is fetched asynchronously from `sdk.privacy-center.org`. Configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is pulled from the Didomi Console at runtime — the loader URL itself is environment-agnostic; the per-environment Notice ID identifies the configuration.
49	- The PWA registers listeners for `consent.changed` and per-vendor status changes. Each gated integration subscribes to the specific purpose or vendor ID it requires; on grant, it dynamically imports or injects its script tag.
50	- SSR HTML must not contain markup whose presence or content depends on consent state — consent-driven UI is hydrated on the client. This keeps the SSR cache consent-agnostic and avoids cumulative layout shift.
51	- No consent rules are hard-coded in the storefront. All configuration (notice copy, purposes, vendors) is owned by the Privacy team in the Didomi Console.
52	
53	## 3. Credentials
54	
55	- **Public credential:** the Didomi Notice ID, embedded in the `@didomi/react` component props. Safe to ship in the browser bundle.
56	- **No machine credential is required from the storefront** — the SDK authenticates using the Notice ID alone.
57	- **Per-environment Notice IDs:** separate Didomi Notices are provisioned per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) so non-production traffic never affects production consent reporting. The PWA reads the active Notice ID from an environment variable resolved at build / runtime.
58	
59	## 4. Data exchanged
60	
61	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| Browser → Didomi | None at runtime — consent UI is rendered by the SDK from the Console configuration | n/a |
64	| Didomi → Browser | Consent state: per-purpose booleans, per-vendor booleans, IAB TCF string, regulation applied, opaque user ID | `consent.changed` event and `Didomi.getCurrentUserStatus()` |
65	| Browser → GTM dataLayer | Default and updated Consent Mode v2 signals | `gtag('consent', 'default' \| 'update', …)` |
66	
67	The storefront does not pass PII to Didomi. The Didomi user ID is an opaque consent identifier — it is not joined to the SFCC customer profile and is never written to the customer record.
68	
69	## 5. Consent and gating contract
70	
71	Every PWA-direct integration that loads a third-party script subscribes to one of the buckets below. The storefront's configurable consent categories are **Performance, Analytics, and Marketing**, with **Required** always granted (REG-051). The exact Didomi purpose IDs used in production are owned by the Privacy team in the Console; the table is the application-side mapping.
72	
73	| Bucket | Purpose family | Scripts gated |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Required (strictly necessary) | Always granted, no banner consent | Didomi itself; SFCC SCAPI; Contentful Delivery API; PWA→MRT proxy reads; Adyen Drop-in — **not Didomi consent-gated**: payment is strictly necessary and the Drop-in loads at the payment step regardless of consent state. The fail-closed rule (§8) applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not payment. |
76	| Analytics / measurement | `analytics`, `measure_content_performance` | GTM analytics tags (GA4 and anything Tell No Lies routes to it); Crazy Egg (all storefronts — AAB-005) and Optimizely Web (US storefront only — AAB-004) — both frontend-direct scripts, not in GTM. **Consent categories are TBC — Zimmermann to confirm** |
77	| Marketing / advertising | `create_ads_profile`, `select_personalized_ads`, `targeted_advertising` | Meta Pixel, GTM marketing tags, Enhanced Conversions |
78	| Performance | `improve_products`, `personalize_content` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD **(TBC)**, Google Maps address autocomplete, Inside Chat **(TBC — consent category to be confirmed with Tell No Lies)**, Omneo widget (vendor disclosure only) |
79	| reCAPTCHA | **EU & UK: consent-gated (TBC)** — loads only post-consent in those regions; no consent required on other storefronts at form interaction | Google reCAPTCHA site-key load on the relevant forms |
80	
81	Adyen is a payment necessity and defers load until the customer reaches checkout, so it does not contribute to LCP on any other page. reCAPTCHA likewise defers until register / login form interaction — it loads with no consent requirement in most regions, and is consent-gated in EU & UK (TBC), providing no bot protection where consent is ignored/declined.
82	
83	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
84	
85	- The Didomi loader is fetched asynchronously and is small (Didomi-reported figures put it in the low single-digit KB range gzipped).
86	- Per HPC-013/014 the Didomi notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes. The underlying LCP candidate (the hero image) still renders behind the scrim, so LCP is measured normally; the page is simply non-interactive until the shopper completes the flow. The grey-out is a confirmed requirement (subject to final designs) — the notice is not deferred away.
87	- All downstream gated scripts are deferred behind their consent callback and dynamically imported / injected. None contribute to the LCP measurement on any page — **with one deliberate, scoped exception: Optimizely Web**. On the US storefront only (per AAB-004), Optimizely is head-loaded before render so its anti-flicker snippet can suppress content flash; this exception is allowed to take priority over the LCP budget. Crazy Egg has no such carve-out and must not block LCP.
88	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to `sdk.privacy-center.org` is emitted in the document head so the SDK fetch does not pay a cold DNS / TLS cost.
89	
90	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
91	
92	- A single Didomi Notice serves all eight storefronts; per-region purpose configuration is managed inside the Didomi Console. The Notice ID does not vary by region — Didomi auto-detects the applicable regulation from the visitor's IP.
93	- Per-region default consent state follows REG-054: EU storefronts opted-out; US domestic requires an explicit choice (no action = opted-out); AU, US international, HK, and ME are opted-in by default. These defaults are configured in the Didomi Console and honoured by the SDK when it loads. The fail-closed rule in §8 applies only when consent state cannot be determined (SDK load failure) and is independent of these per-region defaults.
94	- The marketing opt-in checkbox at registration and newsletter sign-up is **a separate UI control from the Didomi banner** and follows the regional defaults in the Functional Requirements (REG-057): pre-checked on US domestic only, unchecked everywhere else.
95	- The banner language follows the active storefront locale: English for AU, UK, US, HK, ME, and EU international; English, French, Italian, or Spanish for EU domestic. A storefront locale switch triggers `Didomi.setUserLanguage()` so the preference centre also renders in the new language.
96	- **Open (TBD):** consent behaviour on the Global-e-owned checkout iframe origin is not yet settled — how (or whether) Didomi consent state propagates to that cross-origin context remains to be confirmed.
97	
98	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
99	
100	| Failure | Behaviour |
101	|---|---|
102	| Didomi loader fails to fetch (CDN outage, network block, blocker extension) | **Fail closed.** The Didomi Web SDK does not itself default to denied if it fails to load — the storefront implements a 5-second timeout (a project decision, not a Didomi-recommended value). On timeout, the storefront acts as if no consent has been granted: GCM signals stay denied, no gated scripts load. The storefront remains functional for browsing and for SFCC checkout. |
103	| Didomi loader loads but `consent.changed` never fires (SDK initialisation bug, blocked storage) | Same as above — fail closed after the 5-second timeout; the error is logged to monitoring. |
104	| Consent is granted but a downstream script fails to load | The page does not block. The failure is logged. The customer experience continues. |
105	| User revokes consent mid-session | Previously-loaded gated scripts are signalled to disable where the vendor supports it (e.g. GTM `gtag('consent', 'update', …)`). For vendors with no runtime disable, scripts remain in memory but receive no further events; full cleanup happens on the next page navigation. |
106	| User in a region where Didomi has misclassified the regulation | The preference centre is always reachable from the footer "Cookie preferences" link; the customer can adjust manually. |
107	
108	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
109	
110	1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
111	2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.
112

1	# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.
6	
7	> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.
8	
9	The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.
10	
11	In scope at the PWA layer:
12	
13	- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
14	- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
15	- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
16	- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)
17	
18	Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):
19	
20	- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
21	- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
22	- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
23	- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)
24	
25	The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.
26	
27	### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies
28	
29	| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
32	| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
33	| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
34	| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
35	| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |
36	
37	In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.
38	
39	## 2. Vendor relationship
40	
41	- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
42	- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
43	- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.
44	
45	## 3. Browser-side architecture
46	
47	```
48	Page load
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
52	        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
56	        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
57	        │
58	        ▼
59	Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
60	        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
61	        │
62	        ▼
63	GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
64	(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
65	marketing consent is granted
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
69	marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
70	```
71	
72	- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
73	- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
74	- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
79	- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
80	- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.
81	
82	### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)
83	
84	Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.
85	
86	In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
87	```html
88	<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
89	<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
90	new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
91	j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
92	'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
93	})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
94	<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
95	```
96	
97	Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
98	```html
99	<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
100	<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
101	height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
102	<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
103	```
104	
105	> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.
106	
107	## 5. Data layer schema
108	
109	Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.
110	
111	> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.
112	
113	| Event | When | Key fields |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
116	| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
117	| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
118	| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
119	| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
120	| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |
121	| `view_cart` | Cart page load | items[], currency, value |
122	| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
123	| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
124	| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |

1	# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Find My Size** — takes body measurements from the customer, generates a size recommendation, and updates the CTA to display "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050).
8	2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
9	
10	The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
11	
12	In scope:
13	
14	- Script injection on PDP (once on first mount, deferred behind LCP)
15	- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
16	- Detecting data availability via custom events and showing or hiding the trigger accordingly
17	- Updating the product code via the Global Object on SPA navigation
18	- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
19	- Injecting the checkout tracking script on the order confirmation page
20	
21	Out of scope:
22	
23	- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
24	- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
25	- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
26	
27	## 2. How it works
28	
29	```
30	PDP page mounts
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
34	  with data-brand-code, data-product-code (SFCC SKU), data-lang-code, data-country-code
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
38	        │
39	        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
40	        │       │
41	        │       ▼
42	        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
43	        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
44	        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
45	        │   PWA reads event.detail.defaultSize to show "Recommended: Size X"
46	        │
47	        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
48	                PWA shows the Contentful size guide link instead
49	                Customer clicks → PWA renders its own slide-out
50	                                  with Contentful content + cm/in toggle
51	```
52	
53	**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
54	
55	- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
56	- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.
57	
58	Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget.
59	
60	**Confirmed 2026-07-06: Modal Integration is the required path.** The PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between the Measmerize widget and the Contentful size guide fallback); Measmerize is inserted into it via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects Measmerize's HTML directly into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). The `#measmerize-button` div is not used.
61	
62	**Injection pattern:** Inject the script once on first PDP mount inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array. Never place it inside a dynamically re-rendered container.
63	
64	**SPA navigation:** When the customer navigates to a different product (no page reload), update the product code via the Global Object:
65	
66	```js
67	window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU';
68	```
69	
70	`brandCode` cannot be changed at runtime — it requires a page reload.
71	
72	**Modal re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.
73	
74	**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:
75	
76	```
77	GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
78	```
79	
80	Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.
81	
82	**Cleanup:** Remove event listeners and the script element on full component unmount.

84	### Key custom events
85	
86	Events are fired on the script element (`document.getElementById('measmerize-script')`):

88	| Event                           | When it fires                                                  | Payload                                                  |
89	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
90	| `measmerize.script.ready`       | Script loaded with a valid brand code                          | —                                                        |
91	| `measmerize.script.unavailable` | Script loaded with an invalid brand code                       | —                                                        |
92	| `measmerize.widget.ready`       | Widget has data for this product and is about to mount         | —                                                        |
93	| `measmerize.widget.unavailable` | Widget has no data for this product — show Contentful fallback | —                                                        |
94	| `measmerize.widget.recommend`   | A recommendation was generated                                 | `event.detail.defaultSize`, `event.detail.convertedSize` |
95	| `measmerize.widget.addToCart`   | Customer clicked Add to Cart inside the widget                 | `event.detail.size`                                      |

98	
99	| Credential / attribute         | Value                                                                          | Sensitivity   |
100	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
101	| Script URL                     | `https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`                                      | Public        |
102	| Checkout script URL            | `https://client.measmerize.com/checkout.js`                                    | Public        |
103	| `data-brand-code` (staging)    | `b38fac52-7328-45c9-9fd8-038fac4be58e` — shared across Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage | Public        |
